criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The rationale for monitoring the Great Barrier Reef is well argued and referenced with footnotes. However, the mission goals are not converted into quantified requirements (orbit, sensor resolution, revisit, data latency). Users are limited to scientists, with no wider beneficiaries such as reef managers or tourism operators. The concept is clear but lacks specific detail.

evidence.quote: would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A week-by-week Gantt chart with task descriptions and deadlines makes the plan feasible. Information sources are listed. However, there is no explicit contingency or variation provision for slippage, and the plan is only loosely tied to the mission narrative. Sources are listed rather than linked to specific tasks.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
Week 10 is reserved for review, amendments, final simulations, and reflection.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Progress is limited to background reading and STK tutorials. No orbit, launch or simulation results, screenshots or interpretation are presented, so the student cannot yet show technical progress on the mission design. This is minor work completed rather than a useful preliminary result set.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report has a clear section structure, consistent footnoted citations and a labelled Gantt chart. Prose is generally clear. Weaknesses include some awkward phrasing, a cross-reference to a 'next page' that does not match the layout, and the Gantt chart lacking a figure number or caption.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs harbour some of the most diverse species of life on the planet, but this is not even the full extent of their nurture.
Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

technical_issues.quote: current satellites have only mapped Great Barrier Reef depths to a resolution of 100 meters per pixel
technical_issues.issue: The 100 m bathymetry figure comes from a derived depth model, not directly from satellites. The claim is misattributed and needs a precise source.

technical_issues.where: Project Plan & Preliminary Progress (End of Life)
technical_issues.quote: or propelling it out into a graveyard orbit.
technical_issues.issue: Graveyard orbits are a GEO concept. This reef-monitoring satellite is presumably in LEO, so the option is inappropriate without a justified orbit choice.

technical_issues.quote: Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution
technical_issues.issue: Roughly a 30% increase in hydrogen-ion concentration (about 0.1 pH unit) is approximately correct, but the wording should specify the measure and cite it precisely.

technical_issues.quote: Coral reefs harbour some of the most diverse species
technical_issues.issue: No orbit, altitude, launch or sensor parameters are given, so the mission is not yet linked to space-segment course material (R2).

overall: Clear, well-referenced mission rationale and a usable Gantt chart, but the mission requirements are not quantified and there is no technical result to show progress. Contingency planning is absent. Some technical claims need correction. Marks are out of 10 per criterion; weights (40/30/10/20) are applied separately.

feedback.summary: You make a strong, well-referenced case for a Great Barrier Reef monitoring mission, and your Gantt chart and presentation are solid. The gaps are quantification and technical demonstration: requirements are not yet numeric, progress stops at STK tutorials, there is no contingency planning, and a few technical claims need precise sourcing. Marks are unchanged: C1 5/10, C2 6/10, C3 4/10, C4 7/10.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, convert goals into quantified requirements — orbit type and altitude, sensor spatial and spectral resolution, revisit interval, data latency — each traced to a stated user need. Add reef managers, GBRMPA and tourism operators alongside scientists as beneficiaries.

Produce and report a preliminary technical result before submission: choose and justify an orbit (LEO versus GEO — this also makes the graveyard-orbit option in your End of Life section appropriate or replaces it), run an STK coverage or access simulation, and include annotated screenshots with a short interpretation of what the output shows.

Revise the project plan to add contingency and slippage provision (buffer weeks, fallback scope) and map each information source to the specific task it supports. Also correct the 100 m bathymetry attribution and specify precisely what the 30 percent figure measures.
Give the Gantt chart a figure number and caption, tighten awkward phrasing, and check every in-text citation against the reference list.

criteria.C1: Your reef rationale is well argued and footnoted, including sea surface temperature, thermal stress and bathymetry sensing. To reach Accomplished, quantify requirements — orbit, altitude, resolution, revisit, data latency — and widen users beyond scientists to reef managers and tourism operators. Also source the 100 m bathymetry figure precisely (a derived depth model, not direct satellite measurement) and state the acidity measure.
criteria.C2: Your week-by-week Gantt chart with task descriptions and deadlines makes the plan credible, and your information sources are listed. For Accomplished, add explicit contingency and slippage provision (buffer weeks, fallback scope), show why each task sits where it does in the mission narrative, and link each source to the specific task it supports rather than listing them separately.
criteria.C3: Progress currently rests on background reading and STK tutorials 1 to 4. To lift this, present an actual preliminary result: a chosen orbit with altitude and justification, a launch or coverage assessment, and at least one STK simulation with screenshots and a short interpretation of what the output shows and what it implies for the mission.
criteria.C4: Structure, footnoted citations and prose are clear and consistent, and your Gantt chart is legible; this holds at Accomplished. Give the Gantt chart a figure number and caption so it can be cross-referenced, and tighten phrasing such as 'not even the full extent of their nurture'. Check that every in-text citation matches the reference list.
